items.title: Jim Cullum interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: And what Domber was saying this morning was that the music has collective improvisation...

ctx.x: There was some talk this morning about labels and you really do have to label things sometimes. Like Mat Domber’s record label, he calls it classic jazz and we call some things traditional. And sometimes the word “trad” — I wonder if that word doesn’t have some connotations. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-

For some people it does. I’ve had this experience where they say, the people in the crowd, I’ll get off the stage and somebody’ll grab me and say, “When are you going to stop playing that — something besides Dixieland.” And the next person I’ll come to or two or three people over will say, “Well will you please play some Dixieland?” So it depends on your definitions. And what Domber was saying this morning was that the music has collective improvisation that starts sounding like New Orleans, has this what we call…
Yeah. You’ve got to arrange it a little bit more.

items.title: Mat Domber interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 12, 2007
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] ...maybe it was Jim Cullum... [INTERVIEWEE] I think I made that comment.

ctx.x: Yes it is. And it’s cultural as well as musical.

I think, were you saying that — someone this morning was talking about — maybe it was Jim Cullum — that you can’t really separate American culture when you study jazz history. It’s all one and the same.
I think I made that comment.
